title: The Bakery
statementMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7ed0e4643a5b272d27907c9a1f4628457b3331cf.png)

Some time ago Slastyona the Sweetmaid decided to open her own bakery! She bought required ingredients and a wonder-oven which can bake several types of cakes, and opened the bakery.

Soon the expenses started to overcome the income, so Slastyona decided to study the sweets market. She learned it's profitable to pack cakes in boxes, and that the more **distinct** cake types a box contains (let's denote this number as the *value* of the box), the higher price it has.

She needs to change the production technology! The problem is that the oven chooses the cake types on its own and Slastyona can't affect it. However, she knows the types and order of $*n*$ cakes the oven is going to bake today. Slastyona has to pack exactly $*k*$ boxes with cakes today, and she has to put in each box several (at least one) cakes the oven produced one **right after another** (in other words, she has to put in a box a continuous segment of cakes).

Slastyona wants to maximize the total value of all boxes with cakes. Help her determine this maximum possible total value.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*n*$ and $*k*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 35000$, $1 ≤ *k* ≤ *min*(*n*, 50)$) – the number of cakes and the number of boxes, respectively.

The second line contains $*n*$ integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$) – the types of cakes in the order the oven bakes them.

## Output

Print the only integer – the maximum total value of all boxes with cakes.

## Note

In the first example Slastyona has only one box. She has to put all cakes in it, so that there are two types of cakes in the box, so the value is equal to $2$.

In the second example it is profitable to put the first two cakes in the first box, and all the rest in the second. There are two distinct types in the first box, and three in the second box then, so the total value is $5$.
statementZhMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7ed0e4643a5b272d27907c9a1f4628457b3331cf.png)

不久前，甜点女仆 Slastyona 决定开一家属于自己的面包店！她买来了所需的原料和一台可以烘焙多种蛋糕的神奇烤箱，然后开张营业了。

很快，支出开始超过收入，于是 Slastyona 决定研究甜点市场。她了解到，把蛋糕装进盒子里出售是有利可图的，并且一个盒子中包含的**不同**蛋糕种类越多（我们将这个数量称为盒子的*价值*），售价就越高。

她需要改变生产技术！问题在于，烤箱会自行选择蛋糕种类，Slastyona 无法对此产生影响。不过，她知道今天烤箱将要烘焙的 $*n*$ 个蛋糕的种类及顺序。今天，Slastyona 必须恰好将蛋糕装入 $*k*$ 个盒子，并且每个盒子中必须放入烤箱连续烘焙出的若干个（至少一个）蛋糕（换句话说，每个盒子中放入的必须是一段连续的蛋糕）。

Slastyona 想要最大化所有蛋糕盒子的总价值。请帮助她求出这个总价值可能达到的最大值。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*k*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 35000$，$1 ≤ *k* ≤ *min*(*n*, 50)$）——蛋糕数量和盒子数量。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$）——蛋糕种类，按照烤箱烘焙它们的顺序给出。

## 输出格式

输出唯一一个整数——所有蛋糕盒子的总价值的最大值。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，Slastyona 只有一个盒子。她必须把所有蛋糕都放进这个盒子中，因此盒子里有两种蛋糕，其价值等于 $2$。

在第二个样例中，将前两个蛋糕放入第一个盒子、将其余所有蛋糕放入第二个盒子是最优的。此时第一个盒子中有两种不同的蛋糕，第二个盒子中有三种不同的蛋糕，因此总价值为 $5$。
